name: Return on Investment (ROI)
description: Calculate return on investment as a percentage of the cost of investment.
formula: ROI = (Gain from Investment − Cost of Investment) / Cost of Investment × 100
business_contexts: an investor assessing ROI on a portfolio position
a company assessing ROI on a marketing campaign
a manufacturer assessing ROI on a new machine
a retailer assessing ROI on a store remodel
a startup assessing ROI on a growth initiative
question_patterns: Given the gain from investment and cost of investment below, what is the ROI?
Calculate ROI from the figures given.
What is the return on investment, given the gain and cost shown below?
Calculate ROI as a percentage from the gain and cost given.
Using the figures below, what is the ROI?
solution_logic: Step 1: Calculate net gain = gain_from_investment − cost_of_investment
Step 2: Calculate ROI = net gain / cost_of_investment × 100
key_insight: ROI measures net gain relative to what was put in — a positive ROI means the investment returned more than it cost, and a negative one means it didn't.
common_mistakes: Dividing by the gain instead of the cost of investment
Forgetting to subtract the cost of investment before dividing, which reports gross return instead of net
framework_soundbite: ROI is net gain over cost, times 100 — what you got back beyond what you put in, as a percentage.
